newsitem.title: USA: U.S. jobless claims down in latest week.
newsitem.headline: U.S. jobless claims down in latest week.

text.p: U.S. new applications for unemployment benefits fell sharply last week, the Labour Department said Thursday, exceeding the smaller drop that Wall Street had anticipated.

New filings for jobless benefits fell 22,000 to 320,000 in the week ended Oct. 19 from a revised 342,000 in the previous week, the department said. Economists had forecast initial claims of 336,000 in the Oct. 19 week.
The department said initial claims in the week ended October 19 were the lowest since 317,000 in the week ended August 31.
The four-week moving average, which smooths out the often-volatile weekly figures, totalled 331,250 in the latest week, down from a revised 336,250 in the week prior
The department said 11 states reported increases in initial claims exceeding 1,000 on an unadjusted basis in the week ended October 12, the latest period for which the data are available.
Among the largest were Pennsylvania, with 2,878 additional filings; Missouri, with 2,478; Ohio, with 1,896; Minnesota, with 1,581; and Tennessee, with 1,553.
Pennsylvania, Missouri and Ohio cited layoffs in transportation industries. Pennsylvania and Missouri also reported layoffs in the service industry.
Minnesota said its increase was due to the start of the new quarter of wage credits for benefit purposes, as well as layoffs in the automobile industry and in manufacturing.
Tennessee reported layoffs in the food, apparel, chemical, rubber, industrial machinery, transportation equipment, manufacturing and service industries.
Five states reported decreases in initial claims exceeding 1,000 in the latest week.
In the October 12 week Michigan had 3,690 fewer filings, Arkansas had 2,026, Oregon had 1,344, Oklahoma had 1,171, and California had 1,006.
Michigan reported fewer layoffs in various industries. Arkansas had fewer layoffs in the electrical equipment, furniture and fabricated metals industries. The other states had no comment.
